Q: Removing an unused class member slows down program? A:

Your program is a real torture test for the memory system.

You've got an array of 302 (K+2) farly large objects of 4K+4 bytes each (and 4K+8 with the unused head_ member) and iterate over each object performing one computation in each.

    for(int i = 1; i <= K; i++)
        A[i].push_back(A[i-1][j] ^ A[i+1][j]);

The address of A[i].data_[j] is base + i*stride + 4*j, and both the L1 set index and store-load disambiguation only look at the low 12 bits of an address. With stride 0x1004 (4096+4), A[i].data_[j] cache line lands at 4*i mod 4096 (the base + 4*j part is a common constant in the inner loop) - the 302 arrays barely move through the low bits at all.

Issue 1 -- L1 set conflicts. Each inner loop iteration touches one cache line in each of the 302 arrays. With stride 0x1004, those lines' low-12-bit offsets span only 4*302 = 1208 bytes - they crowd into ~19 of the 64 L1 sets, i.e. ~16 lines per set in a 12-way L1 (assuming Alder Lake or newer). The working set (~19 KB) would trivially fit in L1, but associativity conflicts evict lines constantly, so loads that should be L1 hits become L2 hits. With stride 0x1008 the spread doubles (8i, ~38 sets, ~8 lines/set) and just fits 12 ways.

Issue 2 -- 4K aliasing (false store-load dependence). In the inner loop, iteration i loads A[i+1][j] while the store to A[i-1] from two iterations earlier is still in flight. Their address distance is 2*stride − 8:

  • stride 0x1004: 2*0x1004 − 8 = 0x2000 -- an exact multiple of 4096, so the low 12 bits match and the memory pipeline treats every such load as potentially depending on that store. This is worse than a throughput penalty: it serializes the loop, because the store's data came from the previous iteration's loads. This false dependency chain runs through every iteration.

  • stride 0x1008: 2*0x1008 − 8 = 0x2008 -- low bits differ -- no false dependence.

The Fix

Pad the class deliberately instead of relying on an accidental field. 16 extra bytes (stride 0x1010) already beats both versions on my system (i7-12700); stride 0x1040 (one full cache line of low-bit advance per array, cycling through all 64 L1 sets evenly) is the robust choice:

class alignas(64) CyclicArray {

Note - "L2 Bound" in the report is the signal that the data doesn't fit in L1.

One caveat on reading the VTune buckets: with a serializing false dependency, "L2 Bound" cycles and "Store Bound" cycles overlap and the top-down attribution gets murky - the same stalled loads get binned partly as L2 hit latency.

Final thoughts

Obviously the program in the question is contrived, but the actual fix would be to restructure the data and/or the algorithm to process the data in a more sequential way, without gaps. This is called data-oriented design. I think Mike Acton's cppcon talk talk is a great intro into this topic, it's long but is fun to watch.

Q: How to give a font to a option in a Python tkinter.ttk Combobox? A:

Standard Combobox can't display items with different fonts.

It would need to create own widget using Frame with Labels or Buttons which would allow to use different fonts.
It may also need to use Canvas to make it scrollable when there will be more fonts on list.

it seems customtkinter has Combobox which uses tkinter.menu to simulate Dropdown and tkinter.menu can use different fonts for different items.

But it still may need special modifications in this menu.

I created this code which replaces font in every item in dropdown menu using its displayed text.

for index, item in enumerate(combobox._dropdown_menu._values):
    combobox._dropdown_menu.entryconfigure(index, font=(item, 12))

It may need to align text.

I don't know if it will keep font if it would have to redraw all widgets.

Tested on Linux Mint 22.3, Python 3.13, CustonTkinter 5.2.2

Full working code:

import sys
import customtkinter
from tkinter import font

print("Python:", sys.version)
print("CustonTkinter:", customtkinter.__version__)
print("---")

font_names = (
    "Courier New",
    "Arial",
    "Arial Black",
    "Comic Sans MS",
    "Times New Roman",
)

app = customtkinter.CTk()

# after creating Tk()/CTk()
# font_names = font.families()
print(font_names)


def combobox_callback(choice):
    print("combobox dropdown clicked:", choice)


combobox = customtkinter.CTkComboBox(app, values=font_names, command=combobox_callback)
combobox.set(font_names[0])
combobox.pack()

# replace font in every element in dropdown menu
for index, item in enumerate(combobox._dropdown_menu._values):
    print(index, item)
    combobox._dropdown_menu.entryconfigure(index, font=(item, 12))

app.mainloop()

Doc: CTkComboBox | CustomTkinter

Q: In Terminal.app, option+arrow keys no longer move by word A:

I've just bumped into this question and my solution was Terminal.app > Settings (cmd + ,) > Profiles > Keyboard > Use Option as Meta Key. Mind that this is configured per profile.

Option + <arrow> now jumps again word-by-word.

Q: What are Python namespaces all about A:

To understand namespaces, you also have to have some understanding of modules in Python. A module is simply a file containing Python code. This code can be in the form of Python classes, functions, or just a list of names. Each module gets it’s own global namespaces. So you can’t have two classes or two functions in the same module with the same name as they share the namespace of the module.

reference: http://bytebaker.com/2008/07/30/python-namespaces/

Q: Preprocessing image for Tesseract OCR with OpenCV A:

  1. Scanning at 300 dpi (dots per inch) is not officially a standard for OCR (optical character recognition), but it is considered the gold standard.

  2. Converting image to Greyscale improves accuracy in reading text in general.

I have written a module that reads text in Image which in turn process the image for optimum result from OCR, Image Text Reader .

import tempfile

import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

IMAGE_SIZE = 1800
BINARY_THREHOLD = 180

def process_image_for_ocr(file_path):
    # TODO : Implement using opencv
    temp_filename = set_image_dpi(file_path)
    im_new = remove_noise_and_smooth(temp_filename)
    return im_new

def set_image_dpi(file_path):
    im = Image.open(file_path)
    length_x, width_y = im.size
    factor = max(1, int(IMAGE_SIZE / length_x))
    size = factor * length_x, factor * width_y
    # size = (1800, 1800)
    im_resized = im.resize(size, Image.LANCZOS)
    temp_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix='.jpg')
    temp_filename = temp_file.name
    im_resized.save(temp_filename, dpi=(300, 300))
    return temp_filename

def image_smoothening(img):
    ret1, th1 = cv2.threshold(img, BINARY_THREHOLD, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)
    ret2, th2 = cv2.threshold(th1, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    blur = cv2.GaussianBlur(th2, (1, 1), 0)
    ret3, th3 = cv2.threshold(blur, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    return th3

def remove_noise_and_smooth(file_name):
    img = cv2.imread(file_name, 0)
    filtered = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(img.astype(np.uint8), 255, cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_MEAN_C, cv2.THRESH_BINARY, 41,
                                     3)
    kernel = np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8)
    opening = cv2.morphologyEx(filtered, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel)
    closing = cv2.morphologyEx(opening, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)
    img = image_smoothening(img)
    or_image = cv2.bitwise_or(img, closing)
    return or_image

Q: SELECT INTO IN Parameter not possible A:

But I am curious, why is it not permitted to select into p_user_id? Is it not really a variable? Is it a constant?

Yes, an IN parameter is a constant. You can't assign a new value to an IN parameter. You can't use the assignment operator (:=), and neither can you use INTO.

You can declare a parameter as an OUT or IN OUT mode, then assign new values to it.

You can also create a local variable, assign the value of the IN parameter to the local variable, and subsequently change the value of the local variable.

See https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/lnpls/plsql-subprograms.html#GUID-518B8827-26CC-4734-B799-ACB038185638 regarding parameter mode characteristics.

Parameter mode IN

Formal parameter acts like a constant: When the subprogram begins, its value is that of either its actual parameter or default value, and the subprogram cannot change this value.

Actual parameter can be a constant, initialized variable, literal, or expression.

Actual parameter is passed by reference.

(bold emphasis mine)

Q: Wordpress custom css - how to overwrite existing rules A:

Your wordpress theme font family generally is ysabeau-office, but on inspection, the site title is set to another font, literata, and emphasised with !important css, which is what is making it difficult for you to override it. You will have to make your amendment here (to whichever font you want)

The .wp-block-site-title {} css containing the font-family: literata!important; css is at line 3 in the global-styles-inline-css file. The root css that you highlighted will capitalise any font you put in there, so if you don't want it all capitals, the root text-transform line will have to be amended/removed.

Q: What does axis in pandas mean? A:

Let's visualize (you gonna remember always)

In Pandas:

  1. axis=0 means along "indexes". It's a row-wise operation.

Suppose, to perform concat() operation on dataframe1 & dataframe2, we will take dataframe1 and take out 1st row and place into the new DF, then we take out another row from dataframe1 and put into new DF, we repeat this process until we reach the bottom of dataframe1. Then, we do the same process for dataframe2.

Basically, stacking dataframe1 on top of dataframe2 or vice a versa.

Like making a pile of books on a table or floor

  1. axis=1 means along "columns". It's a column-wise operation.

Suppose, to perform concat() operation on dataframe1 & dataframe2, we will take out the 1st complete column (a.k.a 1st series) of dataframe1 and place into new DF, then we take out the second column of dataframe1 and keep adjacent to it (sideways), we have to repeat this operation until all columns are finished. Then, we repeat the same process on dataframe2. Basically, stacking dataframe2 sideways.

Like arranging books on a bookshelf.

More to it, since arrays are better representations to represent a nested n-dimensional structure compared to matrices! so below can help you more to visualize how axis plays an important role when you generalize to more than one dimension. Also, you can actually print/write/draw/visualize any n-dim array but, writing or visualizing the same in a matrix representation (3-dim) is impossible on a paper more than 3-dimensions.
